I have missing videos on my ROVE Dash Cam

ROVE Dash Cam Recording Troubleshooting

I have missing videos on my ROVE dash cam

Missing videos can happen if the camera loses power, the memory card has an issue, the date/time is incorrect, or settings were changed. Use this overnight test to confirm whether your dash cam can record continuously without interruption.

✅ This test helps confirm whether the issue is caused by the camera, memory card, or vehicle power source.

Use stable power

Test the camera at home using a wall USB charger and ROVE's short USB data cable.

Restore defaults

Reset the dash cam to default settings, then set the correct date/time and format the card.

Run an overnight test

Let the camera record overnight, then verify the total trip time and the recorded files in the morning.

Before you begin

Test the dash cam away from the vehicle first

If videos are missing, the fastest way to isolate the cause is to remove the vehicle from the equation. Bring the camera inside your home and power it using a stable wall outlet. This helps confirm whether the camera and memory card can record continuously without car power interruptions.

During this test, do not change extra settings. Keep the setup simple so the result is easier to confirm.

Step-by-step test

Follow these steps in order

Step 1

Stable power test

Power the dash cam at home

Bring the camera inside your home. Use your iPhone or Android phone's USB charger and ROVE's short USB data cable from the box. Plug the camera into your home's 110V wall outlet.

⚠️ Important: Make sure the power does not get interrupted during the test. If power disconnects, the camera may restart or turn off.

Step 2

Playback check

Check video recordings using Playback Mode on the Dash Cam or the ROVE App, including the Events Tab.

Before continuing the overnight test, verify whether videos are actually missing by reviewing recordings directly on the dash cam or through the ROVE App.

How to check videos on the dash cam:

• Press the MODE button until you enter Playback Mode

• Browse through recorded clips using the UP/DOWN buttons

• Open videos and confirm whether recordings are missing or interrupted

✅ Using the ROVE App: Connect to the dash cam WiFi, open the ROVE App, then review videos inside the Album/Playback section.

Step 3

Verify files

Check the memory card on a PC/Mac

Insert the memory card into your PC or Mac and check if all videos were recorded correctly. This helps confirm whether the camera saved clips properly.

What the results mean:

• All videos are recorded: The dash cam and memory card are likely working correctly.

The issue may be related to vehicle power or installation.

• Videos are still missing: The memory card may be faulty, too slow, worn out, or the camera may need further troubleshooting.

Step 4

Reset & prepare

Restore default settings, set date/time, then format the card

If videos are still missing after checking recordings, go to the camera's System Settings and restore the camera to Default Settings. After the camera restarts, set the correct date and time first. Then format the memory card in the camera.

MENU PATH

System Settings → Default Settings → OK

System Settings → Date/Time Setting → Set the correct date and time

System Settings → Format → OK

⚠️ Warning: Formatting the memory card will erase all files, including locked videos, and they cannot be retrieved. Save important footage first.

Step 5

Start recording

Start recording and confirm the red dot/timer

My Camera does NOT Turn ON

ROVE Dash Cam Troubleshooting

My camera does not turn on — here's how to fix it.

Follow these step-by-step options to identify what's preventing your ROVE dash cam from powering on and get back on the road quickly.

Start troubleshooting Contact support

Check the power source

A faulty cable or charger is the most common reason a dash cam won't power on.

Try without memory card

A corrupted or incompatible memory card can sometimes prevent the camera from booting.

Reset the camera

A quick reset with a paper clip can resolve a frozen or unresponsive dash cam.

Before you begin

Bring the camera indoors and use your iPhone or Android smartphone's USB charger along with the short USB cable included in the ROVE box. Plug everything into a standard 110V wall outlet — not your car — to eliminate vehicle power as a variable.

Work through each option below in order. This process helps pinpoint whether the issue is the cable, the charger, or the camera itself.

Step-by-step troubleshooting

Try these options one by one

Option 1

Test with a different USB cable

Swap to the 12FT long L-shaped power cable or the short 1M USB cable — both are included in your ROVE box. Connect it to your smartphone's USB charger and plug it into a wall outlet.

✅ What to look for: If the camera powers on with a different cable, the original cable is defective and needs to be replaced.

Option 2

Remove the memory card

Eject the microSD card from the camera. Unplug the power cable, then plug it back in. Check if the camera powers on without the memory card inserted.

✅ What to look for: If the camera turns on without the card, the memory card may be corrupted or incompatible. Try a new card.

Option 3

Press the Power button once

With the power cable plugged in, press the Power button once. On some ROVE models, the camera does not automatically power on when connected — a single press of the power button is required.

✅ What to look for: The screen should light up within a few seconds of pressing the button.

Option 4

Perform a hard reset

Locate the Reset button at the bottom of the dash cam. Use a straightened paper clip or a pen tip to press and hold the reset button once while the power cord is plugged in.

If the camera still does not turn on, unplug the power cable first, then repeat the reset process.

⚠️ Where to find it: The Reset button is located at the bottom of the camera, near the Serial Number label (R2XXXXXXXXX).

Quick troubleshooting order

Swap cable → Remove memory card → Press Power button → Perform hard reset → Contact ROVE support

Diagnosis Guide

What each test tells you

Camera turns on with a different cable The original USB cable is defective. Contact ROVE support to request a replacement cable under warranty.

Camera turns on without the memory card The microSD card may be corrupted, full, or incompatible. Try formatting the card or replacing it with a new one (Class 10 / U3 recommended).

Camera does not turn on after all options The camera unit itself may be defective. Please reach out to ROVE support — we'll promptly replace any defective item under the warranty to ensure your complete satisfaction.

Still need help? No worries.

At ROVE, your satisfaction means the world to us. Our customer care team is here 7 days a week and will promptly replace any defective item to ensure your complete satisfaction.

Why my video recording has no Audio/Sound

ROVE Dash Cam Audio Troubleshooting

Why does my video recording have no audio or sound?

If your recorded video plays with no sound, the microphone may be muted, the speaker volume may be turned off, or your phone/computer may be playing audio through the wrong output device.

✅ Most audio issues are fixed by turning Record Audio ON and checking playback volume.

Check Microphone

Make sure the microphone icon does not show as muted and that Record Audio is set to ON.

Check Speaker Volume

If Speaker Volume is OFF, playback sound from the dash cam speaker may not be heard.

Check Playback Device

Your phone or computer may be connected to Bluetooth, headphones, or a different audio output.

Visual Guide

Use this guide to locate the microphone and speaker settings

Step-by-step fix

Try these steps in order

Step 1

Start here

What the microphone icons mean:

🎙️ Microphone ON — audio recording is enabled.

🎙️🚫 Microphone OFF — audio recording is muted/disabled.

✅ Quick tip: On many ROVE models, pressing the UP button while recording can mute or unmute the microphone.

Step 2

Camera setting

MENU PATH

Video Settings → Record Audio → ON

⚠️ Important: If Record Audio is set to OFF, newly recorded videos will not include sound.

Step 3

Playback volume

Recommended setting:

Speaker Volume → Med (Default) or High

Avoid using OFF if you want to hear playback from the dash cam speaker.

✅ Note: Speaker Volume affects playback sound, button beep volume, and boot-up chime volume through the camera's built-in speaker.

Step 4

Phone playback

If using the ROVE App, check your phone volume and Bluetooth

When viewing videos from the ROVE App, make sure your smartphone volume is turned up. Also check if your phone is connected to Bluetooth headphones, your vehicle audio system, or another external speaker.

⚠️ Tip: Temporarily turn Bluetooth OFF on your phone and replay the video to confirm the audio is coming from your phone speaker.

Step 5

Computer playback

If using PC/Mac, check the audio output

If the video has audio but you cannot hear it on your computer, make sure your computer's sound output is set to the correct speaker, headphones, or monitor.

Check the following:

• Computer volume is not muted

• Correct speaker/headphone output is selected

• Bluetooth headphones are disconnected if not being used

• Try playing the file in a different media player if needed

Quick Summary

What usually fixes no-audio recordings?

🎙️ Turn Record Audio ON If the microphone was muted, only future recordings after turning it ON will include sound.

🔊 Set Speaker Volume above OFF Use Med (Default) or High so playback sound can be heard from the dash cam speaker.

📱 Check phone/computer audio output Your device may be playing audio through Bluetooth, headphones, or another speaker.

ROVE Troubleshooting Guide

Getting a “Memory Card Too Slow” Error

Learn why your ROVE dash cam displays a “Memory Card Too Slow” warning and follow the troubleshooting steps below to fix the issue.

Why does this error happen?

If your ROVE dash cam displays a “Memory Card Too Slow” message, it usually means the memory card can no longer maintain the required write speed for continuous video recording.

Memory cards have a limited lifespan. Over time, repeated recording and overwriting may cause the card to slow down, develop bad sectors, or become corrupted.

In most cases, this warning means your dash cam is functioning properly and is simply alerting you that the memory card may need maintenance or replacement.

Before you begin

A “Memory Card Too Slow” message usually means the memory card can no longer maintain the required write speed for continuous recording.

In most cases, formatting or replacing the memory card resolves the issue immediately.

STEP 1

Format the Memory Card

Try formatting the memory card using the dash cam settings menu or a computer.

STEP 2

Replace the Memory Card

Replace the memory card with a Class 10 U3 high-speed microSD card recommended for dash cam use.

STEP 3

Upgrade to a High-Speed ROVE Memory Card

ROVE memory cards are specifically designed for continuous dash cam recording and high-performance video writing speeds.

Important Notes

Always safely eject the memory card when using a computer.
Regularly format the memory card inside the dash cam for best performance.
Low-quality or counterfeit cards may cause recording issues.
Replace memory cards periodically depending on recording usage.

text:
My Camera does NOT Turn OFF (Always stays ON)

ROVE Dash Cam — Power Troubleshooting

My camera won't turn off — here's why and how to fix it.

Your dash cam stays on because your vehicle's 12V socket keeps supplying power after the engine turns off. This is a vehicle wiring issue — not a camera defect — and there are 5 ways to fix it.

✅ Your dash cam is working correctly — this is a vehicle power socket issue.

See all 5 solutions Best permanent fix Contact support

"Always hot" socket

Many vehicles keep their 12V cigarette lighter powered even when the engine is off — your dash cam has no way to know the car is parked.

Battery drain risk

A dash cam left on indefinitely while the car is parked can slowly drain your vehicle's battery. Addressing this protects your car.

5 solutions available

From a 2-second button press to a permanent hardwire install — there is a fix for every situation and comfort level.

Why does this happen?

ROVE dash cams are designed to automatically power on and start recording when they receive power, and to shut down automatically when power is removed. This is intentional — it means you never have to touch the camera; it works seamlessly with your ignition.

The issue arises when your vehicle's 12V cigarette lighter socket stays "live" even after the engine is switched off. This is called an "always hot" power source — it's common in many vehicles and is a vehicle wiring characteristic, not a defect in your dash cam.

⚠️ "Always Hot" Socket (your situation)

Power stays ON when engine is off

Dash cam stays ON indefinitely

Risk of draining car battery

Requires one of the 5 solutions below

✅ "Switched" Socket (ideal)

Power cuts when engine is off

Dash cam shuts down automatically

No battery drain risk

No action needed — works as designed

Which solution is right for you?

I want the fastest fix right now — Press the Power button for 2 seconds after parking. → Solution 2

My car has USB ports — Plug the dash cam into a USB port that cuts power with the ignition. → Solution 1

I want a permanent, automatic solution — Install a hardwire kit or re-route the fuse. → Solutions 4 & 5

All solutions

5 ways to fix this — easiest to most permanent

Solution 1

⚡ Easy — No tools needed

Use a vehicle USB port instead

Many modern vehicles have USB ports that automatically cut power when the ignition is turned off — unlike the 12V cigarette lighter socket, which often stays live. Simply swap your dash cam connection from the cigarette lighter to one of these USB ports.

How to test this:

Connect your dash cam's USB power cable to a vehicle USB port (not the cigarette lighter).

Start the vehicle and confirm the dash cam turns on.

Turn off the engine and wait 30 seconds to confirm the dash cam shuts down automatically.

⚠️ Note: Not all vehicle USB ports cut power with the ignition — some are also "always hot." Test by turning the car off and waiting to see if the camera shuts down.

✅ Result: If the camera shuts off when the engine stops, you're done — no further action needed.

Solution 2

⚡ Easiest — Instant fix

Turn off the dash cam manually

The simplest and quickest fix — after turning off your vehicle, press and hold the Power button for 2 seconds to manually shut down the dash cam. This takes just a moment and works on all ROVE models.

HOW TO MANUALLY SHUT DOWN:

Turn off your vehicle

When you turn off the vehicle, simply unplug the USB car charger from the cigarette lighter socket. This immediately cuts all power to the dash cam, causing it to save its final clip and shut down — exactly as designed.

If your vehicle supports it, you can move the fuse powering your 12V socket from an "always hot" fuse slot to a "switched" fuse slot — one that only receives power when the ignition is on. This allows the dash cam to turn on and off automatically with the engine, just as it's designed to.

Install a hardwire kit

The cleanest, most permanent solution. A hardwire kit connects your dash cam directly to your vehicle's fuse box, eliminating the need for a cigarette lighter adapter entirely. The dash cam powers on automatically when the engine starts and shuts off automatically when the engine stops.

Automatically turns ON with ignition

If you're experiencing issues signing in to your ROVE App account—whether it's loading errors, missing verification emails, or registration problems—don't worry. Follow the steps below to troubleshoot and get back on track.

Step 1: Account Registration

Before you can sign in, make sure you’ve registered for a ROVE account.

Step 2: Didn’t Receive Verification Email?

If you didn’t receive a confirmation or verification email during sign-up, try the following:

🔶 Check for Typographical Errors

Double-check the email address you entered during registration for any mistakes.

🔶 Search Your Spam or Junk Folder

Sometimes, automated emails are mistakenly filtered. Search for the sender

🔶 Add to Safe Senders List

To ensure future emails go to your inbox:

• In most email providers (like Outlook), go to Home > Junk > Junk Email Options.

• Under the Safe Senders tab, add [email protected].

🔶 Use a Gmail Account (Recommended)

If issues persist, consider creating or using a Gmail address solely for the ROVE App for better compatibility.

Step 3: App Won’t Load During Login

If the app appears stuck on a loading screen while logging in:

🔶 Close the ROVE App completely (remove it from your background apps).

🔶 Ensure your phone is connected to a stable internet connection (Wi-Fi or cellular).

🔶 Reopen the app and try logging in again.

Step 4: Reinstall the ROVE App

If you’re still facing issues, uninstall and reinstall the app to refresh its performance and connection.

🔶 Download ROVE App for Android:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rovedashcam.android

🔶 Download ROVE App for iPhone:

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rove-dash-cam/id1606959035

Following these steps can resolve most login or sign-up issues quickly. If problems persist, feel free to contact ROVE Customer Support for further assistance—we’re here to help!

Why Is My Dashcam Overheating — What Causes It and How Can I Prevent It?

It’s normal for your ROVE dash cam to feel warm during regular use, especially when recording in 4K, operating in Parking Mode, or running under direct sunlight.

However, if your device becomes unusually hot, shuts down unexpectedly, or displays a high-temperature warning, it may be overheating—and that’s something we want to help you avoid.

1. Extended Exposure to Direct Sunlight

When your vehicle is parked under the sun, especially during summer, cabin temperatures can exceed 140°F (60°C). Prolonged exposure can cause your dash cam’s internal temperature to rise above its normal operating range.

ROVE dash cams are designed to operate between -4°F and 140°F (-20°C to 60°C). To protect itself, the device may slow down, shut off, or stop recording beyond that.

2. Incompatible or Faulty MicroSD Card

A low-quality or non-U3-rated memory card can force the camera’s processor to work harder when saving video files, generating additional heat. Some cards may also fail to write correctly, causing the camera to freeze or overheat.

3. Using Unsupported Power Sources

Power banks, OBD2 adapters, and third-party USB chargers may not supply consistent voltage or include built-in protections. This can cause the dash cam to draw unstable current, increasing heat buildup over time.

4. Parking Mode Running in Extreme Heat

When Parking Mode is active, the dash cam remains on standby or records at a low bitrate while the vehicle is off. Without air circulation or A/C, interior temperatures can spike quickly, increasing the risk of overheating—especially if Parking Mode is left running for long periods.

Here are some practical steps to keep your dash cam running safely and efficiently:
1. Use a High-Quality, U3-Class MicroSD Card

We recommend using a ROVE PRO, ROVE Ultimate, or ROVE Industrial U3 microSD card. These are designed for high-speed 4K recording and maintain stable write speeds, reducing stress on the camera’s processor.

2. Format the Memory Card Regularly

To prevent file system errors and minimize write stress, format your SD card in-camera once every 1-2 weeks.

3. Avoid Direct Sunlight

Whenever possible, park in the shade or use a windshield sunshade to keep the cabin temperature lower. If your vehicle allows, mount the dash cam away from direct sunlight.

4. Use Only ROVE-Approved Power Sources

Use the original ROVE USB-C car charger or the ROVE Ultimate 3-Lead Hardwire Kit for stable and safe operation. These provide a regulated 5V/3.4A output and include built-in protection for your dash cam and your vehicle’s battery.

5. Adjust Parking Mode Settings

If you're in a high-heat region, consider setting a shorter Parking Mode timer (1-3 hours) or disabling it during hotter days. This helps prevent your camera from running too long while the cabin temperature rises.

6. Keep Firmware Up to Date

We release firmware updates to improve performance, fix bugs, and optimize heat management. If you’re unsure of your current version, contact our support team, and we’ll provide the latest version and installation instructions.

Is This Covered Under Warranty?

If your dash cam consistently overheats, shuts off without warning, or displays a “High Temperature” error, it could be a sign of a hardware issue. Please stop using the device and contact us right away. If it’s still under warranty, we’ll work with you on repair or replacement options.

Why can’t I read the license plate number clearly?

ROVE Dash Cam Video Quality Guide

Why can’t I read the license plate number clearly?

License plate clarity depends on lighting, distance, speed, angle, windshield glare, video resolution, and how the video is played back. This guide explains what affects plate readability and how to get the best possible footage from your ROVE dash cam.

✅ For best results, review original video files using VLC Media Player or the ROVE GPS Player.

Lighting matters

Bright glare, darkness, headlights, shadows, and reflections can affect plate readability.

Distance & speed matter

The farther or faster the vehicle is, the harder it is for any dash cam to capture clear plate details.

Use the right player

Windows Media Player may play high-bitrate 4K videos poorly. VLC or ROVE GPS Player is recommended.

Why this happens

License plate capture is affected by real-world driving conditions

Your ROVE dash cam records high-quality video, but reading license plates depends on multiple factors, including proper lighting, focal distance, how close the vehicle is, driving speed, camera angle, glare, reflections, and video playback quality.

For example, a plate may be easy to read when the vehicle is close, centered, and well-lit, but difficult to read if the vehicle is far away, moving quickly, at an angle, or affected by headlights or windshield glare.

Step-by-step improvement guide

How to improve license plate readability

Step 1

Driving conditions

Understand real-world capture limits

License plates are easier to read when the vehicle is close, centered, and moving at a similar speed. Plates may be harder to read when the vehicle is far away, at a sharp angle, moving quickly, or affected by glare, headlights, shadows, rain, or dirty glass.

✅ Best chance for plate capture: Good lighting, close distance, straight angle, clean windshield, and stable playback from the original file.

Step 2

Improve clarity

Clean the windshield and lens

A dirty windshield, a fingerprint on the lens, glare, or reflection can reduce clarity. Clean the windshield area in front of the lens and gently clean the dash cam lens with a soft microfiber cloth.

Step 3

Check playback first

Play the original file using VLC Media Player

Do not judge video quality from a compressed copy, social media upload, text message, or phone preview. Transfer the original video file to your computer and play it using VLC Media Player.

⚠️ Important: Windows Media Player is not recommended for high-bitrate 4K dash cam videos because playback may appear choppy or unclear.

Step 4

Use ROVE GPS Player

Try the ROVE GPS Player

You can also use the ROVE GPS Player from our website to view your videos with Google Maps, G-sensor data, date, direction, and speed during playback.

DOWNLOAD LINK

ROVE GPS Player / Firmware Downloads Page

Quick Summary

What gives you the best chance of reading plates?

▶️ Use VLC or ROVE GPS Player Review the original video file using a player made for high-bitrate video.

💡 Lighting and distance matter most Close distance, good lighting, and a straight angle give the best chance of plate readability.

🧼 Keep the lens and windshield clean Glare, dirt, fingerprints, and windshield reflection can reduce video clarity.

Still need help? We're here.

If you still have issues with the video quality or if you have any other questions about your ROVE dash cam, our support team is available 7 days a week from 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM PST.

Why is my video blurry or out of focus?

ROVE Dash Cam Video Quality Guide

Why is my video blurry or out of focus?

If your dash cam video looks blurry, foggy, hazy, or out of focus, the cause is usually something simple: a protective film, a dirty lens, windshield haze, low-light conditions, or a lower video resolution setting.

✅ Start with the lens and windshield first — they are the most common causes of blurry footage.

Remove lens film

New dash cams may have a clear protective film over the lens that must be removed.

Clean glass and lens

Fingerprints, dust, windshield fog, and interior haze can make footage look soft or cloudy.

Check resolution

Lower recording resolutions will look less detailed than 4K or 2.5K settings.

Before you begin

Blurry video is usually caused by something in front of the lens

The dash cam can only record clearly if the lens and windshield are clear. Protective film, fingerprints, dust, fog, windshield residue, glare, or condensation can all make the video appear blurry even when the camera is working normally.

Follow the steps below in order. After each step, record a short test video in daylight and review the original video file.

Step-by-step fix

How to improve blurry or out-of-focus video

Step 1

Check this first

Remove the protective lens film

Many new dash cams have a clear protective plastic film over the lens. If this film is still attached, videos may look blurry, foggy, or out of focus.

✅ Tip: Check both the front camera lens and rear camera lens if your model includes a rear camera.

Step 2

Clean lens

Clean the dash cam lens

Fingerprints, dust, residue, or smudges can affect video clarity. Gently wipe the lens using a soft, clean microfiber cloth.

⚠️ Important: Do not use harsh chemicals or rough materials on the lens. A soft microfiber cloth is best.

Step 3

Check windshield

Clean the windshield inside and outside

Fog, condensation, dust, dirt, or oily film on the windshield can make the video look hazy or soft. Clean the glass inside and outside, especially the area directly in front of the camera lens.

✅ Best result: Test the camera again in daylight after cleaning the windshield and lens.

Step 4

Low light

Understand low-light video limits

Night driving, very dark scenes, rain, glare, or strong headlights may make the video appear grainy or less sharp. This can be normal in low-light conditions.

What may help:

• Test again during daylight

• Check if HDR is available and enabled on your model

• Avoid placing the camera behind heavy tint or dirty glass

• Adjust exposure if your model supports it

Step 5

Resolution setting

Check the video resolution setting

If the camera is set to a lower resolution, the video will look less detailed. Go to the video settings and select a higher resolution, such as 4K or 2.5K, if your model supports it.

✅ Tip: For the clearest review, transfer the original video file to a computer and play it using a compatible video player.

Quick Summary

What usually fixes blurry or foggy video?

🎞️ Remove protective film Make sure the clear plastic film has been removed from the lens.

🧼 Clean the lens and windshield Smudges, dust, fog, and windshield haze are the most common causes of blurry footage.

🎥 Check resolution and lighting Low resolution or low-light conditions can make footage appear less sharp.

My dashcam is randomly restarting – how to diagnose the issue

If you’re experiencing an issue where your ROVE dash cam keeps turning ON and OFF, it’s likely due to insufficient or unstable power being supplied to the camera. This can be caused by the USB car charger, the USB power cable, or, in rare cases, the dash cam itself.

To help you pinpoint the root cause and get your dash cam back to normal operation, we’ve outlined a few simple troubleshooting steps below:

Start by performing a full reset on the camera. Use a small object like a paperclip or the tip of a pen to press and hold the reset button on the camera. This will clear any temporary glitches and return the camera to its factory settings.

Note: It does not apply to the ROVE R3 dashcam, as it does not have a reset button.

If the issue persists, turn off the camera, remove the memory card, and repeat the test using a 110V wall outlet and both ROVE USB cables.

In some cases, a faulty or corrupted memory card can cause instability in the camera's performance. Testing the camera without the card helps rule out this possibility.

If after trying these steps the issue continues, don’t worry—our support team is here and happy to assist. By narrowing down the potential causes, we can work together to determine whether a replacement part or additional troubleshooting is needed.

We’re committed to helping you get the best performance from your dash cam. If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to reach out!

Dash Cam Repeatedly Turning ON and OFF

ROVE Dash Cam Power Troubleshooting Guide

Dash Cam Repeatedly Turning ON and OFF

If your ROVE dash cam keeps restarting, turning ON and OFF, or cannot stay powered on, the most common cause is unstable or insufficient power. This may come from the USB car charger, USB power cable, vehicle power source, memory card, or in rare cases the dash cam itself.

✅ These steps help isolate whether the issue is caused by power, cable, memory card, or the camera.

Power issue likely

Repeated restarting usually points to unstable power from the outlet, charger, or USB cable.

Test at home

Use a stable wall outlet and phone USB charger to separate camera issues from vehicle power issues.

Check SD card

A corrupted or failing memory card can sometimes cause unstable camera behavior.

Why this happens

The dash cam may not be receiving stable power.

When the camera repeatedly turns ON and OFF, it often means the dash cam is not receiving consistent power. The cause may be the vehicle’s USB/12V outlet, the USB car charger, the USB cable, or a loose connection.

The steps below are designed to narrow down the cause one part at a time so you know whether the issue is coming from the vehicle setup, power accessories, memory card, or the dash cam.

Step-by-step fix

How to troubleshoot repeated restarting?

Step 1

Reset camera

Reset the camera

Use a small object such as a paperclip or the tip of a pen to press the RESET button on the camera. This can clear temporary glitches that may cause the camera to restart repeatedly.

⚠️ Note: The reset button location may vary by model. If your model does not have a reset button, skip this step and continue with the power test.

Step 2

Stable power test

Test the dash cam with a reliable wall power source

Bring the dash cam indoors and plug it into a standard 110V wall outlet using your phone’s USB charger. Test the camera using both ROVE USB cables, if available.

What this test tells you:

• Works normally at home: the issue may be related to your vehicle's power outlet, USB car charger, or vehicle power setup.

• Still restarts at home: continue with the memory card test and cable check.

Step 3

Test both cables

Test with both ROVE USB cables

While testing with the wall outlet, try both the long and short USB cables provided by ROVE. This helps identify whether one cable is loose, damaged, or not providing stable power.

✅ Tip: If the camera only restarts with one cable, replace that cable or contact ROVE Customer Care for the next steps.

Step 4

Memory card test

Remove the memory card and retest

Turn OFF the camera, remove the memory card, then repeat the wall outlet test using both ROVE USB cables. A faulty or corrupted memory card can sometimes cause camera instability.

What the result means:

• Camera works without the card: the memory card may be corrupted, worn out, or incompatible.

• Camera still restarts without the card: the issue may be related to power accessories or the camera itself.

Step 5

Next step

Quick Summary

What usually causes repeated restarting?

🔌 Unstable power The vehicle outlet, USB car charger, or USB cable may not be providing steady power.

💾 Memory card issue A corrupted, worn-out, or incompatible memory card can sometimes cause instability.

🧪 Wall outlet test is important Testing indoors with a stable 110V wall outlet helps separate camera issues from vehicle power issues.

Dash Cam Screen is Frozen

ROVE Dash Cam Troubleshooting Guide

Dash Cam Screen is Frozen

If your dash cam screen is frozen and the buttons are not responding, use the steps below to restart the camera and check whether the issue is caused by power, the memory card, or the camera itself.

✅ Most frozen-screen issues can be cleared by restarting the camera or testing without the memory card.

Restart first

Unplug and reconnect the power cable to reboot the dash cam safely.

Test without SD card

A faulty or slow memory card can sometimes cause freezing or unresponsive behavior.

Reset button note

Some ROVE models have a RESET button. The ROVE R3 does not have a reset button.

What this means

A frozen screen usually means the camera needs to be restarted

If the screen is frozen and no buttons respond, the camera may be stuck temporarily. A quick restart usually clears the issue. If it happens again, the memory card or power source may need to be checked.

Follow the steps below in order. These steps are designed to isolate the most common causes without changing unnecessary settings.

Step-by-step fix

How to fix a frozen dash cam screen

Step 1

Quick restart

Unplug and reconnect the power cable

Remove the power cable from the dash cam, wait a few seconds, then plug it back in. Turn the dash cam ON and check if the screen still freezes.

✅ Tip: A power restart is the fastest way to clear a temporary frozen screen.

Step 2

Reset button

Press the RESET button once, if your model has one

If the screen is still frozen and no buttons respond, press the RESET button at the bottom of the camera once using a paper clip or the tip of a pen. This will restart the camera.

⚠️ ROVE R3 note: This step is not applicable to the ROVE R3 because the R3 does not have a reset button.

Step 3

Memory card test

Remove the memory card and test again

Power OFF the dash cam, remove the memory card, then power the dash cam back ON. Check whether the camera still freezes without the memory card inserted.

What the result means:

• If the camera stops freezing without the card: the memory card may be faulty, too slow, corrupted, or worn out.

• If the camera still freezes without the card: continue troubleshooting or contact ROVE Customer Care.

Step 4

Try another card

Try a spare compatible memory card

If the dash cam works normally without the original memory card, try a spare compatible microSD card. This helps confirm whether the original card is causing the freeze.

✅ Recommended: Use a genuine Class 10 / U3 microSD card. For best reliability, we recommend ROVE PRO, ROVE Ultimate, or ROVE Industrial microSD cards.

Quick Summary

What usually fixes a frozen screen?

🔁 Restart the camera Unplug the power cable and reconnect it to clear a temporary freeze.

📌 Use RESET if applicable Press the RESET button once with a paper clip or pen tip if your model has a reset button.

💾 Check the memory card A faulty, slow, corrupted, or worn-out memory card can cause freezing.
